- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in those periods.
- If model forecast is below true outcome by > 3% for 3+ consecutive days, imply mean reversion; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.
- If model forecast is above true outcome by > 3% for 3+ consecutive days, imply overconfidence; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true trend by 2–5 days; shift forecast 1–3 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often misses the reversal; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift within 2–4 days.
